q: What are causes for secondary peritonitis❓🍒
a:
• #1perforated peptic ulcer + acute appendicitis
  • Ischemic events
    • Bowel infarcition
    • torsion
    • diverticulitis
    • abscess
    • Meckels
    • toxic megacolon
  • trauma (rupture / perforation)
    • GI surgery
  • abscess from all abdominal organs
  • ext. feeding tubes
  • chemical peritonitis (initially sterile)
    • ischemic necrosis of gall bladder (diabetic or septic patient)
    • acute pancreatitis (initially)
    • gastric perforation (initially)

• Pain:
    • abrupt onset
    • continous
    • first localized → diffuse
  • immobile, still, antalgic position

    → slightest movement provoke pain (shallow breathing)

  • wooden abdomen (guarding + rigidity)

    →after time(6-8h) → distension (wodden abdomen disappears)

  • rebound tenderness (blumberg sign)
  • Øbowel sound
  • Bell sign (pain to percussion)
    • typanism if air

  • swollen + painful Douglas pouch on DRE

q: So to sum it all up: Hows the presentation of proximal small bowel obstruction (regarding pain, vomiting, shock, distension, gas+stool passing)🍒
a:
• pain → sudden onset
  • vomiting → early, frequent + profuse

    → fluid-ion loss → early hypovolemic shock

  • initially "flat abdomen"
  • gas + stool emission is possible

• Appendectomy ist the standard (classic/laparo)

  • AB most effective when given preoperatory (decrease post op Infections and abcess formation)

Conservative treatment:

  • Indicated when palpable mass in RIF present

  • AB, bag of ice, fluid diet, surgical observation

  • THEN: If symptoms resolve: appendectomy after 6-8 weeks

 If symptoms progress: urgent appendectomy OR drainage +
later appendectomy

• Necrosectomy and open packing (should be postponed to 3-4 weeks after the acute attack)

  • Planned staged re-laparotomies with repeated lavage

  • Closed continuous lavage of lesser sac and retroperitoneum

  • Closed packing

  • Endoscopic drainage
